claims.text: Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi can serve as a single-phase FCC baseline alloy.
W or Mo is larger than the Mn it replaces in the proposed alloy.
Partial substitution of Mn by W or Mo increases atomic size mismatch in CoCrFeMnNi-based alloys.
Increased atomic size mismatch produces greater local lattice distortion and internal stress fields.
The resulting local strain fields interact more strongly with moving dislocations.
Stronger interaction between local strain fields and dislocations impedes dislocation motion.
Impeded dislocation motion increases hardness and yield strength.
Moderate Mn substitution by W or Mo can retain a single-phase FCC structure.
Within the single-phase FCC regime, increasing substitution will systematically increase local lattice distortion relative to equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
Within the single-phase FCC regime, increasing substitution will systematically increase hardness relative to equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
Within the single-phase FCC regime, increasing substitution will systematically increase yield strength relative to equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
Substitution beyond the solubility limit may produce phase segregation or secondary phases.
Phase segregation or secondary-phase formation may negate the predicted strengthening effect.
The proposed mechanism is limited to compositions that remain single-phase FCC.
Baseline and substituted samples should be processed under identical casting, homogenization, and cold-working conditions.
Hardness, yield strength, local lattice distortion, and phase composition should be measured across a substitution series.
Failure to observe systematic strengthening accompanied by increased lattice distortion in verified single-phase FCC samples would falsify the proposed dominant strengthening mechanism.
